items.stem: A workflow deploys to AWS and must not store long-lived cloud credentials in the repository. Which approach should you use?

options.text: OIDC federation with an id-token permission
options.rationale: Correct: OIDC lets the workflow obtain short-lived cloud credentials with no stored secret.

options.text: A personal access token stored as a repo secret
options.rationale: A PAT is a long-lived credential, which the requirement forbids.

options.text: Hardcoding keys in the workflow YAML
options.rationale: Hardcoding credentials is a severe security anti-pattern.
GITHUB_TOKEN authenticates to GitHub, not AWS, and write-all violates least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: OIDC lets the workflow obtain short-lived cloud credentials with no stored secret.

items.stem: What is the key difference between a starter workflow and a reusable workflow?

options.text: A starter workflow is a scaffold copied into a repo and then independent; a reusable workflow is a central definition invoked via workflow_call
options.rationale: Correct: starter workflows seed new files; reusable workflows are called centrally and stay versioned.
They differ in how they are consumed and maintained.

options.text: A reusable workflow can only run on self-hosted runners
options.rationale: Reusable workflows run on any permitted runner.

options.text: A starter workflow cannot contain jobs
options.rationale: Starter workflows are full workflows with jobs.

items.explanation: Correct: starter workflows seed new files; reusable workflows are called centrally and stay versioned.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of using untrusted third-party actions? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Pin the action to a full commit SHA
options.rationale: Correct: SHA pinning prevents a moved tag from pulling in unexpected code.

options.text: Enforce an organization allow list for actions
options.rationale: Correct: allow lists restrict which actions can run in the org.
Floating @main pulls the latest, possibly malicious, commit.
Broad permissions increase blast radius, not safety.
Disabling logs hinders auditing and does not vet actions.

items.explanation: Correct: SHA pinning prevents a moved tag from pulling in unexpected code. Correct: allow lists restrict which actions can run in the org.
